mercy_translation.text:
It is like a portrait painted on wood that has been obscured by stains from outside. The person whose likeness the portrait bears must come again so that the image may be renewed on the same material. Because of his likeness, even the material on which it is painted is not thrown away; rather, the likeness is restored upon it.

In the same way the all-holy Son of the Father, being the Image of the Father, came to our region so that he might renew the human being made according to him and, as one who had been lost, find him through the forgiveness of sins. As he himself says in the Gospels, “I came to seek and to save what was lost.” For this reason he also said to his own people, “Unless someone is born again”—not meaning another birth from women, as they supposed, but indicating the rebirth and re-creation of the soul according to the image.

And because madness for idols and godlessness held the inhabited world and the knowledge of God was hidden, whose task was it to teach the world about the Father? Would someone say it belonged to a human being? But human beings were not able to travel throughout the entire earth, nor were they by nature strong enough to run so far, nor able to become sufficiently credible in this matter, nor capable by themselves of resisting the deception and illusion of demons.

For since everyone's soul had been struck and disturbed by demonic deception and the vanity of idols, how could a human being persuade the soul and mind of other human beings when they themselves could not even see clearly? How can someone retrain another in what he cannot see?

Perhaps someone might say that creation was sufficient. But if creation had been sufficient, such great evils would not have occurred. Creation was there, and yet human beings continued no less to wallow in the same error concerning God.

Who, then, was needed except the Word of God, who sees both soul and mind, who moves all things in creation, and through them makes the Father known? It belonged to the One who teaches about the Father through his own providence and ordering of the universe to renew that same teaching.

How, then, could this be done? Someone might say that he could do it through the same means and once again reveal the things concerning himself through the works of creation. But this was no longer secure. Human beings had already ignored that way before; they no longer kept their eyes lifted upward but directed them downward.

Therefore, fittingly wishing to benefit human beings, he comes as a human being, taking to himself a body like theirs and working from below, so to speak, through the works of the body. Thus those who were unwilling to know him from his providence and governance of the universe might at least know, from the works done through his body, the Word of God who was in the body, and through him the Father.

translator_notes: Translated directly from the Greek source.
The restored-portrait analogy is one of Athanasius' most important images for renewal in Christ.
The Incarnation is presented as divine pedagogy adapted to humanity's sensory condition.
